hypothesis: An observed return value can instantiate a same-object consumer precondition under an explicit public success contract. Binding and syntax checks construct an executable test without guessing expected scalar values.
algorithm: Enumerate compatible signatures from original repository sources. Ask for only documented success relations. Restore exact source receipts. Insert a consumer after an existing producer/error guard on the same local receiver. Preserve the complete original test.

policy.native_stop: First controlled failure, repeat once; no evaluator-driven replacement.

provider_inputs: Issue, declaration headers and adjacent documentation only; implementation bodies and evaluation findings stay local.
novelty: The producer-consumer form exists in prior work. Investigate the different purpose: create a contract-required successful interaction in an existing test using binding and execution-phase constraints. The present component has narrow Go signatures and no generality evidence.
limitations: A verified quotation proves provenance, not semantic entailment.
A consumer may permit environmental errors or affect later checks. Independent full-test audit remains required.
Preserving original test text can preserve an already-invalid source expectation.
Two APIs can share a wrong implementation assumption and pass their consistency relation.
A timeout alone does not establish a functional defect.
